newsitem.title: GERMANY: Tietmeyer - good chance of German economic recovery.
newsitem.headline: Tietmeyer - good chance of German economic recovery.

text.p: Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer said on Sunday he saw good chances for an economic recovery in Germany and predicted the economy would grow by at least two percent next year.

In a German radio interview, Tietmeyer said two percent growth or more was "certainly possible" for 1997, depending on whether investments picked up pace. He expected 1996 growth of at least one percent.
The main condition for lasting growth was improved investor confidence, the Bundesbank chief said.
"We must become more attractive again for investments from abroad," he said, noting that the outlook for taxes, labour law and wage policies were crucial in this respect.
Wage costs in several sectors would have to rise at a slower rate than productivity to improve firms' competitive positions and ease unemployment.
Tietmeyer also urged a further reduction in budget deficits, predicting that Germany would not meet the Maastricht Treaty criteria on budget deficits this year.
"The deficit in Germany is certainly still too high," he said. The Maastricht Treaty sets a reference level for national budget deficits at three percent of gross domestic product.
The bulk of Tietmeyer's interview, in which he also said he saw no immediate need for interest rate cuts as current levels were not a hindrance to investment, had been released in advance on Friday.
